title: A reasons-first repertoire as Black
origin: map-v1 (OPN.REPERTOIRE.*; the WHITE/BLACK ids are ours)

D0.outcome: Explains that a repertoire is built from the lines the learner actually meets, each ending in a model position with plans and a resulting ending.

D1.outcome: Plays the first eight moves of one reasons-first line as Black against 1.e4 and one against 1.d4, explaining each, and names the model positions and plans.

D2.outcome: Handles the three most common deviations from his own opponents' data in unlabeled positions.

D3.outcome: After twenty own games as Black, revises the repertoire from the opponent-frequency data and writes what changed and why.

sources: sources/sheets/edlasker_chess-strategy.md §4 K8, K11 (keep the option of ...d5); §5 item 2
conditions: Every line ends at a model position with plans and a link to the resulting endgame.
Black's central break ...d5 is the standard equalising break and should not be prevented by early moves.
contrasts: An early move that lets White prevent the central break.
note: Map id was OPN.REPERTOIRE.*; split into WHITE and BLACK.
